text_blocks.snippet: Pubic lice, also known as crabs, are treated with medicated creams or lotions containing permethrin or pyrethrins and piperonyl butoxide. These can be found over-the-counter or prescribed by a doctor. Treatment typically involves applying the medication to the affected area, leaving it on for a specified time, and then washing it off. A second treatment may be needed a week later to kill any newly hatched lice.
snippet_highlighted_words: medicated creams or lotions containing permethrin or pyrethrins and piperonyl butoxide

list.title: Over-the-counter medications:
list.snippet: Permethrin cream (e.g., Nix) and pyrethrins with piperonyl butoxide mousse are commonly used, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

list.title: Prescription medications:
list.snippet: Malathion lotion is a prescription option, applied for 8-12 hours and then washed off.

list.title: Eyelash treatment:
list.snippet: For pubic lice on eyelashes, a special ointment may be prescribed and applied twice a day for several days, says healthdirect.

list.title: Home care:
list.snippet: In addition to medication, washing clothes and bedding in hot water is crucial to prevent re-infestation.
Follow instructions: Carefully follow the instructions on the medication label.
Retreatment: A second treatment may be necessary to kill lice that hatch after the initial treatment.
Sexual partners: Sex partners should be checked and treated to prevent re-infestation.
Other STIs: People with pubic lice should also be checked for other sexually transmitted infections.
Consult a doctor: If over-the-counter treatments don't work or if you have concerns, consult a doctor or pharmacist, according to healthdirect.
